suggestions.issue: The bullet 'a pressure antinode coincides with a velocity antinode — for sound, pressure maxima line up with velocity minima' introduces the unexplained concept of a 'velocity antinode' to an intermediate PA learner. Since the rest of the term only ever works in terms of pressure, this adds cognitive load and a new jargon pair with no scaffolding or payoff for the studio/live-sound use cases.
suggestions.suggestion: Either add a half-clause gloss (e.g., '...where air movement, not pressure, is greatest') or drop this bullet and keep the correction focused on the node/antinode confusion, which is the misconception a room-mode learner will actually hit.

suggestions.issue: This term is tagged 'beginner', but purpose_function and common_mistakes introduce 'spectral (pinna) cues' with no gloss. For a beginner the word 'pinna' and the phrase 'spectral cues' are unexplained prerequisites, so a learner meeting this term first cannot decode why front/back and height differ from left/right.
suggestions.suggestion: Add a two-word gloss on first use, e.g., 'spectral cues from the outer-ear (pinna) shape', so the beginner can attach meaning before the same terms reappear in common_mistakes.
